Trigger: When finalizing a yes/no chest X-ray finding answer and a question-specific tool such as chest_xray_expert returns “yes,” or phrase grounding returns the target phrase with a bounding box, but a broad grounded report contains only a related negative such as “no focal lung parenchymal nodule,” or the ROI visual impression seems normal.

Verification action: Before changing the direct positive result to “No,” search the current same-image observations for an explicit negation of the exact object and attribute asked about—e.g., “no mass” or “no mass in the lungs.” Do not treat “no focal nodule,” “no abnormality of the pulmonary vessels,” or a subjective normal-looking ROI impression as equivalent exclusion evidence. If no explicit same-image negation exists, retain the supported positive answer or report the conflict as unresolved. If choices are displayed, map the supported answer text back to the displayed option and confirm its letter and text agree. In this case, chest_xray_expert answered “yes” and xray_phrase_grounding localized “mass” in the right lower lobe; maira2_grounded_report only said “no focal lung parenchymal nodule.” The terminal “No” converted a related negative into an exclusion of mass and contradicted the direct positive evidence, while the released reference was “yes.”

Trigger: Before finalizing a yes/no chest-radiograph answer about a specific finding such as “Is a pneumothorax present in the left apex?”, after a direct same-question image tool and/or grounded report has already returned evidence.

Verification action: Check the direct current-image tool output for the exact object and attribute, then compare it with any same-finding statement in the grounded report and with the terminal answer’s polarity. In this case, chest_xray_expert answered “No” to “Is there a pneumothorax in the left apex?”, and maira2_grounded_report stated “There is no evidence of pneumothorax”; the terminal answer “No” matched both. If options are displayed, map the supported text back to the displayed option and confirm the letter and text agree. If the tool and report conflict, resolve the conflict or report uncertainty rather than asserting. Do not treat a correct grade alone as proof of the procedure, and do not rely on a bare visual-inspection claim unless the observation is actually available.

Trigger: Before finalizing a yes/no chest-radiograph answer about a focal finding (e.g., hilar lymphadenopathy) when two tools have already been consulted and the direct same-question VQA tool and the grounded-report tool return opposite polarity.

Verification action: Compare the two observations at the level of the exact object and attribute, and check whether the negative line in the grounded report is a generic template statement or an actual localized finding. In the supplied case, chest_xray_expert was asked "Is there hilar lymphadenopathy in this chest X-ray?" and returned "yes," while maira2_grounded_report emitted "No evidence of hilar adenopathy" with an empty boxes array (boxes: [])—the same negative phrasing the report uses for mediastinal adenopathy and other normal structures, and the report itself carries the "Unverified findings" limitation. The terminal answer "No" silently adopted the report's negative line and discarded the direct same-question "yes," with no reconciliation; the reference is "yes," so this is a wrong conclusion, not an option-mapping error (no options were displayed). The reusable procedure: when a direct same-question tool answer conflicts with a grounded-report line, do not default to the report's negative just because it is phrased as a normal finding—either identify observable evidence that resolves the conflict (e.g., a grounded box on the hila) or report the conflict as unresolved instead of asserting a bare "No." A same-question direct answer that is contradicted must be addressed, not omitted from the rationale. If options are displayed, map the supported answer text back to the choice and check that letter and text agree.
